newsitem.title: USA: Irvine Sensors CEO outlines strategy.
newsitem.headline: Irvine Sensors CEO outlines strategy.

text.p: Irvine Sensors Corp's new chief executive, James Evert, on Wednesday outlined his corporate strategy beginning with improving Irvine Sensor's finances and capitalizing on its technology.
Evert was named chief executive of the high-technology producer of electronics, image processing and sensing devices.

"My first priority is to improve the company's financial performance," Evert said in a statement. "This is challenging since we now have a high fixed-cost in our Vermont operation. Furthermore, our backlog is not yet large enough to produce consistent financial performance from quarter to quarter."

Evert said the company's backlog of work is not large enough for consistent financial results quarter to quarter, and its Vermont products continue to suffer because they require high-volume production to be cost effective.

The company recently received a $3.2 million order from Lockheed Martin Corp's Federaly Systems division for Vermont. Still, Evert said if it can't produce Vermont in high volumes soon, "I will not hesitate to redeploy our resources."
One bright spot in Irvine Sensor's outlook is its subsidiary, Novalog, which is "positioned for significant growth" in 1997's second half, Evert said.

To address its problems, Sensor has set about reducing expenses by over $500,000 and cutting staff in many of its operations. It is boosting its marketing activity to produce revenue growth and bring in new business.
"Newly formed teams have just completed business plans for three products in development," Evert said.

These products are the Real Time Vector Image Processor, a board-level system using silicon neuron technology; the Silicon MicroRing Gyro, a micro-machined sensor; and Electronic Film, a combination of technologies that allows digital photography without a digital camera.

Evert said he did not know exactly how Sensor would exploit the new products but said the establishment of a separate subsidiary "has proven quite successful for Novalog." Novalog sells Irvine's wireless infrared technology.
"Whether or not new product initiatives become the basis of new subsidiaries, strategic alliances or licensing agreements will be determined on a case-by-case basis," he said.
